title: Separated finite-type Cartesian diagonal neighbourhood of a coordinate chart
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:X\to Y$ smooth, separated, of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open [def-weil-open-immersion], and $e:U\to A=\mathbf A^d_Y$ etale over $Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Put $p:A\to Y$ and $h=fj=pe$. The schemes $Y,X,U,A$ are Noetherian, $h$ and $e$ are separated of finite type, and every indicated open inclusion is quasi-compact and of finite type. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, put $X_V=f^{-1}V$, $U_V=U\cap X_V$, $A_V=\mathbf A^d_V$. The schemes $V,X_V,U_V,A_V$, $U_V\times_VU_V$ and $A_V\times_VA_V$ are separated finite type over $k$; the maps $X_V\to V$, $U_V\to V$, $A_V\to V$ and the first and second projections from each displayed product are smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. No absolute separatedness of $Y$ is assumed.

For such $V$, write $W=U_V\times_VU_V$, $W_A=A_V\times_VA_V$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $Z=U_V\times_{A_V}U_V\subseteq W$, and let $\Delta_U,\Delta_A$ be the diagonals [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The section $\Delta_U:U_V\to Z$ is open and closed, so $Z\setminus\Delta_U(U_V)$ is closed in $W$. Its complement $O$ is an open neighbourhood of the diagonal. The restriction $q=(e_V\times e_V)|_O:O\to W_A$ is etale, and
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U_V&\xrightarrow{\Delta_U}&O\\
e_V\downarrow&&\downarrow q\\
A_V&\xrightarrow{\Delta_A}&W_A\end{array}$$
is Cartesian as a square of schemes. The map $p_U:O\to U_V$ induced by the first projection is smooth separated of finite type and dimension $d$, with closed section $\Delta_U$. The factorization $O\xrightarrow{(p_U,e_Vp_{2,U})}U_V\times_VA_V\xrightarrow{(e_V,1)}W_A$ has first arrow etale over $U_V$ and second arrow the base change along $e_V$; the inverse image of the graph section $u\mapsto(u,e_Vu)$ under the first arrow is precisely $\Delta_U$. All its schemes are separated finite type over $k$.

proof.text: Apply the Mathlib finite-type-over-Noetherian results to aY and f. Open subschemes of Noetherian schemes are locally Noetherian and compact. The Mathlib instance quasiCompact_of_noetherianSpace_source proves quasi-compactness of every morphism from these Noetherian sources, in particular the open inclusions. Open immersions are locally of finite type. Composition gives their structure morphisms finite type.

proof.text: The affine-space projection is affine and smooth of relative dimension d, hence separated and of finite type. Consequently A is Noetherian. The open immersion U into X and f are separated, so h is separated; separated cancellation in e followed by p gives separatedness of e. The etale e is locally of finite type, and its Noetherian source gives quasi-compactness directly.

Base change preserves separated finite-type morphisms by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; apply this to $f,h,p,e$ along $V\to Y$ (for $e$ equivalently along $A_V\to A$), and to $U_V\to V$, $A_V\to V$ along themselves for the product projections. Since $V$ is affine, its morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Composing separated and finite-type maps using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] proves that $V,X_V,U_V,A_V,W,W_A$ are separated finite type over $k$. In particular the products are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Their open subschemes and open inclusions have the finiteness properties of Step 1.

Mathlib identifies etale with SmoothOfRelativeDimension 0. Apply this to U into X and compose with f, obtaining relative dimension 0+d=d for h. AffineSpace.smoothOfRelativeDimension_over supplies dimension d for p. Base change gives fV,hV,pV and both projections from W and WA the claimed relative dimensions. The same dimension-zero composition proves the assertion for the projection from O.

proof.text: Mathlib pullback_map_diagonal_isPullback identifies Z with the inverse image of the diagonal of AV under ee. Its map z is closed by the existing separated mapDesc instance. The diagonal i of eV is open by etaleness and closed by separatedness. Therefore z maps the closed complement of its range to a closed set. Define O as the complement of this exact image. Injectivity of z proves z^{-1}(O)=range(i). The open-immersion lifting property constructs delta, and IsOpenImmersion.isPullback proves its square with i, O into W and z Cartesian.

proof.text: The canonical morphisms of pullbacks changing one leg give the Cartesian squares for r and s (isPullback_pullback_map and isPullback_pullback_map_left). Hence r,s,ee=r followed by s and the restriction of ee to O are etale. Paste the Cartesian open-cut square with pullback_map_diagonal_isPullback. Simplifying the diagonal projection gives exactly IsPullback delta eV (O.ι followed by ee) (diagonal pV).

Separatedness of b makes its diagonal closed; cancellation along O.ι proves delta closed. Its composite with the first projection is the identity. Noetherianity of W makes O.ι quasi-compact, and open immersions are locally of finite type and separated. Compose to obtain all finiteness and separation assertions. The graph square before restriction is proved directly by the universal property of pullback eV eV: a test cone determines the two morphisms to UV and equality of their eV-composites, and uniqueness follows from the projections. Paste it with the open-cut square to obtain the graph square over O. Base change and composition give the properties of every listed structure morphism. No nonemptiness or positive-dimension assumption is used.

Every off-chapter node it cites is on the route of sk-prop-sp-orientation (sk-def-smooth, sk-thm-vanishing, sk-thm-p1) or is a Mathlib leaf, so the two declared tool_uses are on route and accepted. Steps 1-3, 5, 6 and 7 are correct. Step 1: Noetherian opens, qc and finite-type inclusions. Step 2: p affine and separated; e separated by cancellation, and of finite type by nagata (b) since p is separated; absolute separatedness of Y is never used. Step 3: base change along V→Y, with e_V the base change of e because U_V=e⁻¹(A_V). Step 5: Z≅W×_{W_A}A_V, the diagonal of the étale, separated e_V is clopen, and C is closed in W. Step 6: each factor of e_V×e_V is a base change of e_V, and O×_{W_A}A_V=Z∩O=Δ_U(U_V) as schemes. Step 7: closed section, p_U separated and of finite type, and the graph's inverse image is Z∩O=Δ_U. Edge cases checked: d=0 with two sheets (the off-diagonal components are removed), e an open immersion (O=W), empty V, and a non-separated Y.
